item.title: UK authorizes military to board Russian shadow fleet tankers
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Wednesday that he has given the military and law enforcement agencies permission to board and detain Russian shadow fleet vessels in British waters, escalating the United Kingdom's campaign to cut off oil revenues funding Moscow's war in Ukraine.

The decision marks the first time the UK has authorized its own forces to directly intercept the sanctioned tankers, after months of supporting allied operations led by the United States and France. Starmer framed the move as a response to rising oil prices driven by the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, warning that Russian President Vladimir Putin was "rubbing his hands" at the prospect of higher energy revenues.

item.title: France rules out military action to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu told the National Assembly on Wednesday that France will not take part in military operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force, drawing a firm line even as energy executives and central bankers warned that fuel shortages and faster inflation are heading for Europe within weeks.

item.title: Thai tanker crosses Strait of Hormuz fee-free after Tehran diplomacy
item.description: A crude oil tanker owned by Bangchak Corporation safely transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday after diplomatic talks between Thailand and Iran, becoming one of the few vessels to pass through the near-shuttered waterway without paying a toll that has reportedly reached as much as $2 million per voyage.

item.title: Iran allows fuel tankers through Hormuz in goodwill gesture to US amid war
item.description: The "present" that President Donald Trump said Iran gave the United States was the safe passage of several fuel tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, a senior Arab diplomat and a US official told The Times of Israel on Wednesday. The gesture came as Washington tested whether a diplomatic off-ramp to the nearly month-long war was possible, with Trump postponing threatened strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure.

item.title: Iran demands Lebanon be included in any ceasefire deal
item.description:
Iran has told intermediaries that Lebanon must be part of any ceasefire agreement with the United States and Israel, linking an end to the nearly month-long war to a halt in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah, according to a Reuters report citing six regional sources familiar with Tehran's position.

The demand, communicated to mediators as early as mid-March, adds a layer of complexity to nascent and indirect diplomatic exchanges between Washington and Tehran as the conflict approaches its fourth week with no clear path to resolution.

item.title: Iran drafts law to formalize tolls on Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran's parliament is advancing legislation to charge ships transit fees for passing through the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing what has already become an informal toll system on one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints. The plan is expected to be finalized next week, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

"We are pursuing a proposal in which Iran's sovereignty, control, and oversight in the Strait of Hormuz are formally recognized in law, and through the collection of tolls, a source of revenue is also created for the country," an unnamed lawmaker told Fars. Tehran lawmaker Somayeh Rafiei earlier told the ISNA news agency that countries using the strait for shipping, energy transit, and food supply chains would be required to pay fees to Iran.

item.title: Artemis 2 crew flies to Florida ahead of April 1 Moon launch
item.description: Four astronauts are one week away from launching on a journey around the Moon, the first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years. NASA is targeting April 1 at 6:24 p.m. EDT for liftoff of the Artemis 2 mission from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, sending Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch of NASA, along with Canadian Space Agency Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen, on a 10-day flight around the far side of the Moon and back to Earth.

item.title: Iran says it will weigh U.S. ceasefire proposal as markets watch
item.description: Global markets treaded cautiously on Thursday as investors weighed conflicting signals from Middle East ceasefire negotiations, with Iran indicating it would consider a U.S. proposal to end the Gulf conflict even as fighting continued. Asian stocks struggled for direction in early trading, while oil prices remained elevated and the dollar held firm near recent highs.

item.title: Asian stocks waver as Iran sets five conditions for ceasefire
item.description: Wall Street rallied on Wednesday while oil prices pulled back after the Trump administration delivered a 15-point ceasefire proposal to Iran, injecting cautious optimism into markets rattled by nearly a month of conflict in the Middle East. But gains faded through the session as Iran publicly rejected the diplomatic overture, leaving investors navigating a volatile landscape heading into Thursday's Asian trading.

item.title: Oil prices rebound as Iran reviews US peace plan
item.description:
Oil prices climbed on Thursday as Iran indicated it was still reviewing a 15-point peace proposal from the United States aimed at ending the Middle East conflict that has disrupted global energy flows for nearly a month. The rebound followed a sharp selloff a day earlier when news of the diplomatic overture first emerged.

Brent crude rose to around $103 a barrel in Thursday morning trading, according to the Independent, recovering part of Wednesday's roughly 4% decline. The previous session's drop came after reports surfaced that the U.S. had transmitted the proposal to Tehran through Pakistan, briefly raising hopes of de-escalation.

item.title: Asian stocks slide as Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan
item.description: Asian stocks fell and oil prices climbed on Thursday as Tehran's rejection of a U.S. ceasefire proposal dashed hopes for a swift end to the Iran war, now in its fourth week.

item.title: Southeast Asia turns to nuclear power to fuel AI data center boom
item.description:
Several Southeast Asian nations are resurrecting long-shelved nuclear energy programs as the region races to meet surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence data centers, with the ongoing war in Iran adding urgency by disrupting global energy supplies and driving up fossil fuel costs.

Five of the ten members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations — Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines — are now actively pursuing nuclear power, with nearly half the region potentially incorporating nuclear energy by the 2030s, according to the Associated Press. The push coincides with a broader global movement in which nearly 40 countries have pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050.

item.title: Iran quietly reviews US ceasefire plan despite public rejection
item.description: Iran is still reviewing a 15-point American proposal to end the war in the Persian Gulf despite publicly dismissing it, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, as oil prices rebounded from earlier losses and gold climbed on persistent uncertainty over the conflict's trajectory.

item.title: Rice researchers recover 95% of battery metals using plasma and citric acid
item.description: Researchers at Rice University have developed a new method for recycling lithium-ion batteries that recovers nearly 95 percent of valuable metals using microwave-induced plasma and citric acid — the same acid found in lemons. The patented process, published in the journal Advanced Materials, offers a lower-energy, less chemically intensive alternative to current industrial recycling techniques.

item.title: Gold slides, oil holds above $100 as Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan
item.description: Gold fell below $4,500 per ounce on Thursday morning while oil prices remained elevated above $100 a barrel as markets digested the collapse of a U.S. ceasefire proposal to Iran and the ongoing military conflict across the Middle East.

item.title: IBM says quantum computer matched lab data in materials simulation
item.description: IBM announced on Thursday that its quantum computer has accurately simulated the behavior of a real magnetic material, producing results that match neutron scattering experiments conducted at national laboratories. The achievement, which researchers say was previously considered beyond the reach of current quantum hardware, marks a turning point in the effort to use quantum computers as practical tools for scientific discovery.

item.title: Dollar slips in Asia as Iran diplomacy doubts dim Fed hike bets
item.description:
The U.S. dollar edged lower in Asian trading on Thursday as investors sought clarity on whether diplomatic efforts could bring a de-escalation in the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, while scaling back expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes later this year.

The U.S. dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, slipped 0.1% after posting its largest one-day gain in a week during the prior session. The dollar remained near 99.5, below the ten-month highs reached earlier in March when the conflict first sent energy prices surging.

item.title: Israel strikes Isfahan as Iran fires missiles at Tel Aviv
item.description:
Israel launched a series of strikes on Iranian military and nuclear facilities around Isfahan on Thursday, as Iran retaliated with two missile barrages targeting central Israel, marking another day of escalation in a nearly month-long war even as President Donald Trump insists Tehran is ready to negotiate.

The Israel Defense Forces said they had completed strikes on what they called critical infrastructure in Isfahan, a city that hosts a major air base and nuclear sites previously targeted during the conflict. Iran responded with missile volleys that activated air raid sirens in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, with rescue teams dispatched to impact sites in central Israel. An Israeli soldier was also killed by rocket fire from Lebanon, where Hezbollah has been launching attacks since early March.

item.title: OECD warns U.S. inflation could hit 4.2% amid Iran war oil shock
item.description: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned Thursday that US headline inflation could reach 4.2% in 2026, sharply higher than its previous estimate of 3%, as the ongoing US-Israel military conflict with Iran sends global energy prices soaring. The revised projection, published in the OECD's interim economic outlook, is more than double the Federal Reserve's 2% target and marks one of the steepest upward revisions the organization has made in a single quarter.

item.title: IRGC Navy chief killed in Israeli strike on Bandar Abbas
item.description:
Israel killed the commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy, Alireza Tangsiri, in a strike on the southern Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas, an Israeli official told The Jerusalem Post on Thursday. The killing of Tangsiri, who oversaw Iranian naval operations near the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints, marks a further escalation in the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28. Iranian authorities had not publicly confirmed the killing as of Thursday morning.

The strike came as Iranian ballistic missiles continued to target Israel, with sirens sounding across central Israel on Thursday morning. The IDF said it detected and intercepted an Iranian missile launch targeting central Israel, while six people were lightly wounded across two separate barrages earlier in the day. An 11-year-old girl in Safed suffered cardiac arrest during an air-raid siren and was hospitalized in serious condition.
